title: Understanding Internet Services and URL Structure
description: Explore internet services like email, web browsing, and e-governance while learning URL anatomy
objective: Students will analyze URL structures, explore internet services including email and e-governance portals, and understand how different protocols serve different purposes

steps.title: Break Down URL Structure
steps.instructions:
A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a web page. Let us learn to read URLs by breaking them into parts.

**Open Chrome and visit:** `https://www.irctc.co.in/nget/train-search`

Now break this URL into parts:
```
https://www.irctc.co.in/nget/train-search
|_____| |_| |____| |___| |________________|
  |      |     |     |          |
  |      |     |     |        Path (specific page)
  |      |     |   TLD (Top-Level Domain: .co.in = commercial India)
  |      |   Domain (irctc = website name)
  |    Subdomain (www = World Wide Web)
Protocol (https = secure connection)
```

**Now practice with these URLs. Fill in the table:**

| URL | Protocol | Domain | TLD | Path |
|-----|----------|--------|-----|------|
| https://www.google.com/search?q=CCC | | | | |
| https://www.digilocker.gov.in/dashboard | | | | |
| https://mail.google.com/mail/inbox | | | | |
| https://student.nielit.gov.in | | | | |
| http://example.com/page.html | | | | |

**Common TLDs (Top-Level Domains) in India:**
- `.com` = Commercial
- `.gov.in` = Indian Government
- `.co.in` = Commercial India
- `.ac.in` = Academic India
- `.org` = Organization
- `.edu` = Education

**Security Check:** Which URLs above use HTTP (not secure) vs HTTPS (secure)? How can you tell the difference in your browser?

**CCC Exam Connection:** URL = Uniform Resource Locator. Know the parts: protocol, domain, TLD, path.

steps.title: Explore Email Services
steps.instructions:
Email is one of the most important internet services. Let us explore how it works.

**Step A: Understand an email address**
```
rahul.sharma@gmail.com
|___________| |_______|
  Username    Domain
      |
  @ (at symbol - introduced by Ray Tomlinson in 1971)
```

**Step B: Open Gmail (or any email service)**
1. Open Chrome and go to https://mail.google.com
2. Log in to your email account (or use the training account provided)

**Step C: Compose an email**
1. Click **Compose** (or the + button)
2. Fill in these fields:
   - **To:** (your partner's email address)
   - **Subject:** CCC Lab 05 - Email Practice
   - **Body:** Write a short message about what you learned in the networking topic
3. Click **Send**

**Step D: Understand email fields**
| Field | Purpose | Example |
|-------|---------|--------|
| To | Main recipient | amit@gmail.com |
| CC | Carbon Copy (visible to all) | sneha@gmail.com |
| BCC | Blind Carbon Copy (hidden from others) | trainer@techpath.biz |
| Subject | Topic of the email | Lab submission |
| Attachment | Files attached to the email | report.pdf |

**Step E: Check the Spam folder**
1. In Gmail, click on **Spam** in the left sidebar
2. Notice the types of emails that Gmail automatically detected as spam
3. Why are these marked as spam?

**CCC Exam Connection:**
- SMTP = Protocol for SENDING email
- POP3 = Protocol for RECEIVING email (downloads to device)
- IMAP = Protocol for RECEIVING email (keeps on server, syncs across devices)
- CC is visible to all recipients; BCC is hidden

steps.title: Compare Internet Services and Protocols
steps.instructions:
Different internet services use different protocols. Let us understand which service uses which protocol.

**Step A: Fill in this table from what you have learned:**

| Internet Service | Protocol Used | Example | Port Number |
|-----------------|---------------|---------|------------|
| Web Browsing (secure) | ___ | Chrome visiting google.com | 443 |
| Web Browsing (not secure) | ___ | Old websites without padlock | 80 |
| Sending Email | ___ | Clicking Send in Gmail | 25 |
| Receiving Email | ___ or ___ | Checking inbox | 110 or 143 |
| File Transfer | ___ | Uploading files to server | 21 |
| Remote Access (secure) | ___ | Managing a server remotely | 22 |
| Domain to IP conversion | ___ | Typing google.com in browser | 53 |

**Step B: Observe protocols in action**
1. Open Chrome and visit: `http://example.com` (notice: HTTP, not HTTPS)
2. Now visit: `https://www.google.com` (notice: HTTPS)
3. In the address bar, do you see a difference?
   - HTTP site: What does the browser show? (Warning? Padlock?) _______________
   - HTTPS site: What does the browser show? _______________

**Step C: Check what protocol your email uses**
1. When you sent email in Step 2, Gmail used SMTP to send it
2. When your partner received it, Gmail used IMAP to deliver it to their inbox
3. You did not see these protocols — they work behind the scenes!

**Step D: Protocol matching exercise (practice for exam)**
Match each service with its protocol:
1. Browsing a secure website → ___
2. Sending an email → ___
3. Downloading a file from a server → ___
4. Converting google.com to an IP address → ___
5. Remote login to a server (secure) → ___

Answers: HTTPS, SMTP, FTP, DNS, SSH

**CCC Exam Connection:** Knowing which protocol does what is essential for the exam. SMTP sends email, HTTPS is secure browsing, FTP transfers files.

steps.title: Internet Security Awareness Check
steps.instructions:
Let us test your ability to identify internet threats and practice safe browsing.

**Step A: Identify phishing**
Look at these email examples and decide which are real and which are phishing:

| Email | From Address | Subject | Real or Phishing? |
|-------|-------------|---------|------------------|
| 1 | support@sbi.co.in | Your monthly statement | |
| 2 | sbi-support@secure-login.com | Your account is blocked! Click here NOW! | |
| 3 | noreply@irctc.co.in | Your ticket booking confirmation | |
| 4 | irctc.refund@gmail.com | Claim your refund of Rs 5000 immediately | |

**How to identify phishing:**
- Check the sender's email domain carefully
- Look for urgency ("NOW!", "immediately", "account blocked")
- Banks and government sites never ask for passwords via email
- Look for spelling mistakes

**Step B: Check your browser security settings**
1. Open Chrome Settings (three dots > Settings)
2. Go to **Privacy and Security**
3. Check these settings:
   - Is **Safe Browsing** turned on? ___
   - Are **Cookies** set to block third-party? ___
   - Is **Send a Do Not Track request** enabled? ___

**Step C: Test password strength**
Visit a password strength checker or evaluate these passwords:
| Password | Length | Uppercase | Lowercase | Numbers | Special | Strong? |
|----------|--------|-----------|-----------|---------|---------|--------|
| 123456 | 6 | No | No | Yes | No | |
| Password123 | 11 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | |
| T3ch@Path2026! | 14 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | |
| priya | 5 | No | Yes | No | No | |

**Step D: Know where to report**
1. Open: https://cybercrime.gov.in
2. What types of crimes can you report here?
   - _______________
   - _______________
   - _______________
3. Helpline for financial fraud: _______________

**Summary — Write a paragraph (5-6 sentences) about what you learned today about internet safety.**

**Take a screenshot of your completed tables and submit with your lab report.**
